history.text: Portuguese navigators found the islands uninhabited.
Sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans made the islands briefly the world's largest producer.
Cocoa and coffee replaced sugar under the roca estate system.
The first multi-party elections were held.

worthSeeing.title: Pico Cao Grande:
worthSeeing.text: A volcanic plug rising some 300 m from the forest.

worthSeeing.title: Obo National Park:
worthSeeing.text: Rainforest covering much of both islands, rich in endemic birds.

worthSeeing.title: Roca Agua Ize:
worthSeeing.text: A colonial-era plantation estate with its hospital and rail remains.
